text:
Blake Lizotte is an undrafted, 5'9" centre who has lasted more than 400 NHL games by doing the small jobs well: killing penalties, blocking shots, winning his shifts. This season he has no goals in 18 games, and that number deserves context more than criticism.

He has 2.42 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and zero to show for them, which is about as unlucky as a depth forward gets in a month and a half. Meanwhile, his line has played well. The Penguins have taken 55% of the expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, better than when he sits, and he has five assists. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he's more of a setup man than his reputation: 8.2 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 84th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey had him slightly above replacement, mostly for defence. One goal will come, probably off something ugly in front. The real question for him is whether a selling team still has a job for a bottom-six centre, and so far his play says yes.
